item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 081726
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Thu Oct 8 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Rachel, located several hundred miles west of the southern tip
of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Simon,
located a couple of hundred miles off the coast of southwestern
Mexico.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form south of the coast of
Guatemala early next week. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for some gradual development of this system thereafter, and a
tropical depression could form as it moves generally
west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Simon are issued under WMO
header WTPZ35 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Simon are issued under WMO
header WTPZ25 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 47
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026 
647 
WTPZ33 KNHC 082051
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number  47
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026
 
...RACHEL WEAKENS SLIGHTLY...
...EXPECTED TO TURN NORTHEASTWARD AND HEAD TOWARD BAJA CALIFORNIA 
ON FRIDAY...
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.4N 124.6W
ABOUT 935 MI...1510 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...987 MB...29.15 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in extreme northern Baja California, northern Gulf of
California, and southern California should monitor the progress of
Rachel. Tropical Storm Watches could be required for a portion of
this area tonight.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was 
located near latitude 22.4 North, longitude 124.6 West. Rachel is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 3 mph (6 km/h). This general 
motion is expected to continue over the next 24 hours, before a 
sharp turn to the northeast, along with an increase in forward 
speed, occurs on Friday and Saturday. On the forecast track the 
center of Rachel is expected to approach the northern portion of 
Baja California late Saturday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Gradual weakening is expected over the couple of days, but 
Rachel is still expected to be at tropical storm strength when it 
approaches northern Baja California.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 987 mb (29.15 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header
WTPZ43 KNHC.

RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain to portions of 
Baja California this weekend.

Rachel and the moisture associated with the system will also bring 
rainfall of 1 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5 
inches across the higher terrain, across portions of the Southwest 
United States this weekend. This will lead to increasing coverage of 
rainfall and potential for flash and urban flooding.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with 
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall 
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and 
the Flash Flood Risk graphic at 
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.

SURF: Swells partly generated by Rachel will build along the coast
of Southern California and northern Baja California through the
weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions as well as minor to moderate coastal 
flooding.  Please consult products from your local weather office.

WIND: The risk of tropical-storm-force winds is increasing 
for portions of northern Baja California through extreme 
northwestern Mexico this weekend, and a Tropical Storm Watch may be 
required for a portion of that area later tonight. Strong gusty 
winds associated with the system are expected to spread over 
interior portions of the Southwest United States, especially in 
areas of higher terrain, from this weekend into early next week.
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Brown

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 46
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 081446
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  46
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026

Rachel's satellite presentation continues to slowly degrade as dry 
air continues to affect the cyclone. The coldest cloud tops are 
around -50 C. The most recent TAFB subjective Dvorak intensity 
estimate is still a 4.0/65 kt, while the objective estimates from 
UW-CIMSS are in the range of 33-56 kt. Based on the available data, 
the initial intensity has been held at 60 kt for this advisory. 

The initial motion was estimated at 300/6 kt. The cyclone is still 
being steered by the high pressure anchored over the southwestern 
United States. In about a day or so, a mid- to upper-level trough 
currently sweeping across the Pacific is expected to turn Rachel to 
the northeast and increase the forward speed of the storm as well. 
The spread in the track guidance has decreased, so there is a bit 
more confidence in the track forecast. The current NHC track is 
mostly the same as the track prior, only a few minor adjustments to 
the east have been made based on the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids. 
 
The gradual weakening tread for Rachel is expected to continue as 
the storm continues to move through an environment characterized by 
cooling sea-surface temperatures and dry mid-level air. Wind shear 
is expected to increase over Rachel as the previously mentioned 
trough approaches the system, which will help to weaken the storm 
further. However, the sea-surface temperatures are warmer than 
normal for the waters near California and Baja California and the 
interaction of the trough could help foster the growth of convection 
as well.  There is still a high degree of uncertainty on if Rachel 
will be a tropical or post-tropical system as it approaches northern 
Baja California and southern California. Regardless, the cyclone is 
expected to produce heavy rainfall and tropical-storm-force winds. 
The current NHC intensity forecast remains unchanged from the 
previous advisory.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rachel is expected to approach the coast of extreme northern 
Baja California, northern Gulf of California, and Southern 
California at tropical storm strength over the weekend, potentially 
bringing strong winds and coastal flooding to portions of those 
areas. A Tropical Storm Watch could be required for a portion of 
this area by tonight. Gusty winds are likely to spread over interior 
portions of the Southwest United States into early next week.

2. Moisture associated with Rachel will spread over portions of the 
Southwest United States and northern Baja California peninsula 
through this weekend. This will lead to increasing coverage of 
rainfall and a threat of flash and urban flooding.

3. Swells partly generated by Rachel will build along the coast of 
Southern California and northern Baja California through the 
weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and 
rip current conditions.  Please consult products from your local 
weather office.

 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Thu Oct 08 2026 
000

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Simon Advisory Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 PM CST Thu Oct 08 2026
 
...SIMON ALMOST A HURRICANE...
...HURRICANE WARNING ISSUED FOR SOUTHWESTERN AND WEST-CENTRAL 
MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.7N 103.9W
ABOUT 230 MI...370 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 345 MI...555 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...992 MB...29.30 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
The government of Mexico has issued a Hurricane Warning from Punta
San Telmo to Playa Perula and a Tropical Storm Watch from Lazaro
Cardenas to Punta San Telmo.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* West of Playa Perula to Punta Mita
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued
36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Additional watches or warnings could be required for portions of the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico tonight or Friday.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor products 
issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Simon was 
located near latitude 15.7 North, longitude 103.9 West. Simon is 
moving toward the west near 6 mph (9 km/h). A turn to the northwest 
is expected by early Friday, followed by a northward motion Friday 
night. On the forecast track, the core of Simon is expected to 
approach the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico on 
Saturday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Rapid strengthening is forecast, and Simon is 
expected to become a hurricane tonight and a very dangerous category 
4 hurricane before it reaches the coast of Mexico.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 992 mb (29.30 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND:  Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area
Saturday afternoon or evening, with tropical storm conditions
expected Saturday morning. Hurricane conditions are possible within
the hurricane watch area by Saturday night, with tropical storm
conditions beginning on Saturday. Tropical storm conditions are
possible within the tropical storm watch area beginning Friday.
 
RAINFALL:  Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 8 to 15
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals between 15 and 25 inches possible across portions of
Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco through Sunday. This rainfall may
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE:  A dangerous storm surge is possible along the 
immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes 
landfall. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and 
destructive waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 600 PM CST.
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Simon Forecast Discussion Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Thu Oct 08 2026 
225 
WTPZ45 KNHC 082032
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Storm Simon Discussion Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 PM CST Thu Oct 08 2026
 
Simon is almost a hurricane. The storm continues to have a very 
compact inner core with some signs of an eye becoming apparent in 
satellite images. There are also numerous spiral bands beyond the 
inner core region, with the outermost band in the far northeast 
quadrant still affecting portions of southwestern Mexico. The latest 
satellite intensity estimates have increased a little from earlier 
and now range from about 50 to 65 kt. Based on that data, the 
initial intensity is nudged up to 60 kt. A 17Z ASCAT-C pass was used 
to adjust the initial wind radii.
 
The tropical storm is moving slowly westward at about 5 kt, steered 
by a weak mid-level ridge to its north. A turn to the northwest is 
expected tonight or early Friday, followed by a northward motion 
later that day when the ridge weakens and shifts eastward, in 
response to an approaching mid- to upper-level trough. Although the 
models generally agree on the large-scale steering pattern 
evolution, there are very important differences in where and when 
the system makes that turn. There has been a notable shift to the 
east this cycle, and given the westward bias often seen in the 
models for this region, the NHC track forecast has been again nudged 
eastward. It should be noted that the best-performing models of the 
year so far are east of the official forecast, and additional 
adjustments might be needed if this trend continues. This forecast 
brings the core of the system inland over southwestern and 
west-central Mexico Saturday afternoon or Saturday night.
 
Simon is in near ideal environmental conditions of low wind shear,
high moisture, and over very warm waters. The SHIPS model shows more
than a 70 percent chance that the system will rapidly intensify over
the next 24 hours. In fact, the storm's compact inner core structure
makes it even more likely that it will capitalize on the favorable
conditions. Therefore, the NHC intensity forecast continues to call
for rapid strengthening into a very dangerous category 4 hurricane
before Simon reaches the coast of west-central Mexico. This forecast
lies near the high end of the guidance, in best agreement with the
HCCA model.
 
Based on the new forecast, the government of Mexico has issued a 
Hurricane Warning for a portion of the coast of southwestern and 
west-central Mexico.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Simon is expected to strengthen to a hurricane by tonight and 
approach the west-central coast of Mexico as a major hurricane on 
Saturday.

2. Life-threatening wind and storm surge impacts are expected along 
a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a Hurricane 
Warning is now in effect from Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula. 
Preparations to protect life and property should be completed by 
late Friday.

3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.

4. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central 
coast of Mexico through the weekend. These swells are likely to 
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please 
consult products from your local weather office.
